\chapter{Chapter05 — Two Div Pi}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.TwoDivPi}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Uniform measure on the Boolean cube]
\lean{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p023-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b002
}
\label{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformPMF}
For a nonnegative integer $n$, take the uniform probability measure on the
$n$-dimensional Boolean cube, assigning equal probability to every point.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Weighted Rademacher summand]
\lean{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b008,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b002
}
\label{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.signValue}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a$ assign a real number $a_i$ to each coordinate
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x$ be a point of the Boolean cube. For each coordinate
$i$, the corresponding summand is $a_i$ multiplied by the sign of the $i$th coordinate
of $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of signed linear-form terms]
\lean{FABL.sum_twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\label{FABL.sum_twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.linearForm, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a_1,\\ldots,a_n$ be real numbers, and let $x$ be a
point in the $n$-dimensional sign cube. The sum over $i=1,\\ldots,n$ of $a_i$ times the
$i$th sign coordinate of $x$ equals the linear form $\\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product representation of the sign measure]
\lean{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure_eq_pi}
\label{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure_eq_pi}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformSample_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the uniform probability measure on the set of sign vectors
of length $n$ equals the product, over the $n$ coordinates, of the uniform probability
measure on the two signs $-1$ and $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a Rademacher coordinate]
\lean{FABL.integral_twoDivPiSignCoordinate_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.integral_twoDivPiSignCoordinate_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.integral_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and choose $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ uniformly. For every coordinate
$i$, the mean of the sign in that coordinate is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a Rademacher summand]
\lean{FABL.integral_twoDivPiRademacherSummand_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.integral_twoDivPiRademacherSummand_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.integral_twoDivPiSignCoordinate_eq_zero, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a=(a_i)_{i=1}^n$ be a vector of real numbers, and
choose a sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ uniformly. For each coordinate $i$, the mean of
$a_i x_i$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Independence of Rademacher summands]
\lean{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummands_iIndep}
\label{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummands_iIndep}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure_eq_pi, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $a_1,dots,a_n$ be real numbers. On the uniform
probability space of sign vectors $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the random variables $a_i x_i$, for
$1\le i\le n$, are mutually independent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability of a Rademacher summand]
\lean{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand_memLp}
\label{FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand_memLp}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a$ be a real-valued function on the $n$ coordinates,
let $i$ be one of those coordinates, and let $p$ be an extended nonnegative real number.
Under the uniform measure on sign vectors of length $n$, the function sending a sign
vector $x$ to $a(i)$ times its sign at coordinate $i$ belongs to $L^p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance of a Rademacher summand]
\lean{FABL.variance_twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\label{FABL.variance_twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.integral_twoDivPiRademacherSummand_eq_zero, FABL.integral_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, every coefficient vector $a\in\bbr^n$, and every
coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the variance under the uniform measure on $\{-1,1\}^n$
of the random variable $x\mapsto a_i x_i$ is $a_i^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform measure of an event]
\lean{FABL.twoDivPiUniformMeasure_real_event}
\label{FABL.twoDivPiUniformMeasure_real_event}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.integral_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be any decidable property of sign vectors
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The probability of the event $\{x:P(x)\}$ under the uniform measure on
sign vectors equals the uniform probability of $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the standard Gaussian density]
\lean{FABL.gaussianPDFReal_zero_one_le_one}
\label{FABL.gaussianPDFReal_zero_one_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $x$, the standard Gaussian density at $x$ is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian mass of a symmetric interval]
\lean{FABL.gaussianReal_real_Icc_neg_le_two_mul}
\label{FABL.gaussianReal_real_Icc_neg_le_two_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.gaussianPDFReal_zero_one_le_one}
\difficulty{4}
For every $t\ge 0$, the standard Gaussian measure of the interval $[-t,t]$ is at most
$2t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Small interval probability for a linear form]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_abs_linearForm_le}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_abs_linearForm_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RealInterval.toSet, FABL.exercise5_16_interval, FABL.gaussianReal_real_Icc_neg_le_two_mul, FABL.integral_twoDivPiRademacherSummand_eq_zero, FABL.linearForm, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one, FABL.sum_integral_abs_cube_le_of_ae_abs_le, FABL.sum_twoDivPiRademacherSummand, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherMeasure, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummand_memLp, FABL.twoDivPiRademacherSummands_iIndep, FABL.twoDivPiUniformMeasure_real_event, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.variance_twoDivPiRademacherSummand}
\difficulty{5}
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be real numbers with $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\le\delta$
for every $i$, and let $t\ge0$. For a uniformly chosen sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the
probability that $\left|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\right|\le t$ is at most $2t+2C\delta$,
where $C$ is the third-moment Berry–Esseen constant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation against a linear form]
\lean{FABL.expect_mul_linearForm_eq}
\label{FABL.expect_mul_linearForm_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.linearForm, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, and let $a$ assign a real coefficient to each coordinate. The uniform
expectation of $f(x)$ times the linear form $sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$ equals $sum_{i=1}^n
a_i\widehat f(\{i\})$, where $\widehat f(\{i\})$ is the uniform expectation of
$f(x)x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For every sign $s\\in\\{-1,1\\}$ and real number $z$, let $\\operatorname{sgn}_0(z)$ be
$1$ when $z\\ge0$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then $(\\operatorname{sgn}_0(z)-s)z$ equals $2|z|$
if $s\\ne\\operatorname{sgn}_0(z)$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.thresholdSign_gap_eq}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p113-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function from the $n$-dimensional sign
cube to $\{-1,1\}$, and let $\ell$ be a real-valued function on that cube. For $t\geq0$,
define the threshold sign to be $1$ when its argument is nonnegative and $-1$ otherwise.
Then $2t$ times the uniform probability that $f(x)$ differs from the threshold sign of
$\ell(x)$, minus the uniform probability that $|\ell(x)|\leq t$, is at most
$\mathbb{E}[(\operatorname{sign}(\ell(x))-f(x))\ell(x)]$, where the expectation is
uniform on the cube and $\operatorname{sign}(\ell(x))$ denotes that threshold sign.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{7}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every dimension $n$, every Boolean function $f$
on the sign cube, and every $0<\varepsilon\le1$ for which each level-one Fourier
coefficient has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$ and the total Fourier weight at
level one is at least $2/\pi-\varepsilon$, the relative Hamming distance from $f$ to the
sign of its degree-one Fourier part is at most $C\sqrt{\varepsilon}$.
\end{theorem}
